slides: Now, let's go to the other end of the essay... the closing paragraph.
So what is the closing paragraph for? For the essay, we want to sum it up.
For the rater, it also sums things up. But we also want to avoid mistakes. What do I mean by that?
Well, by the time the rater gets to your closing, they already have your score in mind. For content, and for language.
Your content score, your critical thinking, that's measured in the body. The arguments, the weakenings, the opposing arguments, and how you deal with them.
And language? They've read a whole essay, they know where you stand. At most you can give it a small bite. A phrase, or a word or two, that fits most closings.
So all you need to do here is... no mistakes. No embarrassing slips.
It's actually not by accident that we teach the opening and the closing last. After arguments, weakenings and the rebuttal.
They're the bread of the sandwich. Inside is everything we actually want to make. But we need a slice on top and a slice below to hold it, or the sandwich falls apart.
So the opening is on top, the closing is below. And the filling is what gives the taste... and the score.
So what do we do in the closing? We sum up the essay. Things we've already written.
The opening takes its content from the task text. The closing takes its content from the essay itself.

So you don't need to reinvent the wheel. Go to the relevant paragraphs. There are real pieces of sentences there that build the closing, like Lego. And in the next lesson, I'll show you exactly which ones.
We don't bring new arguments. There's no new content in a closing.
Even if you suddenly think of an argument that seems really, really good... don't.
Because then you've added an argument with no support. The rater won't think 'oh, a good argument'. They'll see a claim with no support, and it hurts you.
I also don't bring the opposing argument back again. The one from the rebuttal paragraph.
I want to leave the rater with a good taste. They've already read the opposing argument, and they've seen me weaken it. Done.
So, let's sum up: I support the cameras because of A, and because of B. Goodbye.
The score has already been set. Just don't make mistakes. That's all.
